statusVocabulary.established: Previously established mathematics, cited to external literature.
statusVocabulary.prior-art: Capability or limitation documented by an earlier software system.
statusVocabulary.repository-audit: Direct observation about the canonical repository at the audit commit.
statusVocabulary.definition: Repository-specific mathematical definition; not asserted as prior art or theorem.
statusVocabulary.proved: Theorem proved in the PolyTwist monograph from stated assumptions.
statusVocabulary.proved-example: Exact example claim proved by symbolic algebra or explicit witnesses in the monograph.
statusVocabulary.computational-evidence: Deterministic experiment or computation, not promoted to theorem.
statusVocabulary.open: Explicitly unresolved research or algorithm-design problem.

claims.statement: Semialgebraic sets are closed under Boolean operations, projection, closure, and taking connected components; each semialgebraic set has finitely many connected components.
Finite semialgebraic families admit compatible finite semialgebraic triangulations or cell decompositions.
Semialgebraic mappings admit finite local-triviality decompositions of the target.
Finite affine hyperplane arrangements partition Euclidean space into a finite face complex whose face counts are controlled combinatorially.
The sign vectors of an affine hyperplane arrangement are the covectors of a realizable oriented matroid after homogenization; oriented matroids retain combinatorial but not metric information.
An arrangement of n hyperplanes in fixed dimension d can be constructed in optimal O(n^d) time in the classical model used by the cited arrangement algorithm.
First-order formulas over real closed fields admit quantifier elimination; cylindrical algebraic decomposition is one constructive route.
Cylindrical algebraic decomposition constructs sign-invariant connected cells and can provide adjacency information through later refinements.
Real quantifier elimination and CAD have doubly-exponential worst-case lower-bound phenomena in the general variable-count regime.
Rigid-body placement and collision constraints can be represented as regions and obstacles in configuration space.
Exact motion planning can be formulated through connectivity and topology of semialgebraic configuration spaces.
Partial bijections and partial group actions are canonically related to inverse semigroup actions.
Partial actions admit universal globalization results under the hypotheses developed in the cited work.
Expected reduction in posterior entropy is a classical measure of information supplied by an experiment.
Classical Rubik-type puzzle families already possess substantial group-theoretic and algorithmic complexity results; PolyTwist does not claim novelty for that baseline.
Twizzle/cubing.js PuzzleGeometry derives permutation, SVG, and 3D representations from symmetric flat cuts of Platonic solids.
Twizzle's first-party documentation states that its PuzzleGeometry model does not support bandaging or jumbling.
KPuzzle is a permutation-and-orientation execution representation rather than a complete geometric mechanism definition.
Magic Puzzle Ultimate already permits user-defined symmetry groups, axes, cutting planes, twists, and body boundaries, including higher-dimensional puzzles.

At the audit commit, the compiler is restricted to cubic logical sizes 2 through 9, three orthogonal coordinate families in one transformed frame, convex half-space cells, and quarter-turn generators.
At the audit commit, state-dependent legality is implemented only through exact logical layer selection and rigid bandage closure, not swept geometric collision.

The existing research ledger already separates established, provisional, and open claims, but its Slice-Action Code and Unified Legality Operator remain provisional and do not define a general mechanism.
A Stratified Kinematic Atlas is the exact tuple (K; B, Phi, beta, J, T, O) introduced in the monograph.
The canonical cut stratification uses connected components of every ternary sign condition, not sign vectors alone.
A visible mechanical seam is the boundary trace of a cut carrier after quotienting away interfaces whose adjacent chambers belong to the same bonded physical piece.
Physical pieces are admissible bond components of atomic chambers, represented as regular closures of their chamber unions.
The continuous configuration space is the quotient of exact rigid placements satisfying nonpenetration, anchor, joint, and clearance constraints; docked states form a distinguished subset.
A turn template consists of a state-indexed anchor frame, an exact gate, a semialgebraic rigid-motion path, and a docking predicate.
A turn is legal exactly when gate atomicity, bond closure, swept-path admissibility, and endpoint docking all hold.
The legal-motion structure is the inverse semigroup generated by reversible partial turn maps together with its associated action groupoid on docked states.

An exact atlas isomorphism is an orientation-preserving rigid equivalence with compatible relabelings that preserve body, oriented cuts, bonds, assembly data, turn templates, and declared observations.
The connected sign-component stratification is finite under the monograph's semialgebraic regularity assumptions.
For a convex body cut by affine hyperplanes, every nonempty strict sign region is convex and connected, so strict sign vectors index atomic chambers without a component suffix.

For an affine cut and a polyhedral boundary face, the trace segment, endpoints, length, orientation, and incidence are obtained by one exact line computation followed by interval clipping against the face inequalities.
The same body and cut stratification can support nonisomorphic legal-motion systems; therefore cuts alone cannot be the canonical puzzle definition.
A binary chamber selector respects every bond exactly when its support vector lies in the kernel of the oriented incidence matrix of the bond graph.
Under the atlas definitions, legal turn execution factors into four independent proof obligations: gate, bond, path, and docking.
When all atlas data and motion paths are semialgebraic, each turn domain is semialgebraic.
A reversible turn template induces a partial bijection of docked state space, with inverse induced by the reversed path.
The partial bijections generated by reversible turn templates form an inverse subsemigroup of the symmetric inverse monoid on docked states.
If every primitive turn is legal at every docked state, the inverse-semigroup dynamics reduce to an ordinary group action and the labeled state graph becomes a Schreier graph.
A finite semialgebraic turn family induces a finite connected semialgebraic stratification of docked state space on which the legal action mask is constant.
An exact atlas isomorphism induces isomorphic cut incidence, congruent physical pieces, conjugate partial actions, and isomorphic labeled state graphs.
Boundary cut traces at one state do not identify an internal mechanism: an interior closed cut can change chamber and action structure while leaving every boundary trace unchanged.
A finite state graph with a finite-memory scramble policy is represented exactly by a product automaton; finite-horizon laws are matrix products and rational policies produce rational probabilities.

A finite hypothesis class is exactly identifiable by finite experiments iff every pair of hypotheses is separated by at least one admissible experiment outcome; optimal worst-case identification depth equals the minimum separating decision-tree depth.
Rational Ghost Atlas A has an exact orthogonal mechanism frame, twenty-seven witnessed strict chambers, and six explicitly clipped traces on the selected boundary face.

Rational Ghost Atlas B has an exact orthogonal mechanism frame, twenty-seven witnessed strict chambers, and five explicitly clipped traces on the selected boundary face, with one carrier invisible on that face.

For bounded-degree algebraic atlases with finite symmetry groups, there exists a practical exact canonical-labeling pipeline whose output is stable under rigid atlas isomorphism and polynomial in output size for generic instances.
Develop output-sensitive exact collision certificates specialized to axial polyhedral turns, avoiding generic CAD on ordinary puzzle instances while retaining a quantifier-elimination fallback.
Characterize which atlas equivalence classes are identifiable from passive multi-view images, from legal-action queries, and from active visual interaction under occlusion and unknown appearance.
Develop practical proof-carrying connected-component and incidence compilation for curved and nonconvex bounded-degree semialgebraic cut carriers.
Define robust exact semantics for kerf, clearance, compliance, contact, and manufacturing tolerance, together with a sound robust-legality theorem.
Determine which exact invariants of the legal-motion groupoid predict planning and active-identification difficulty without degenerating into arbitrary benchmark feature engineering.
